name: Basilica of St. Louis, King of France
history: St. Louis's founders set aside this land for the Church in the 1760s; a log church was blessed here in 1770. The present limestone church, built from 1831 to 1834, was the first cathedral west of the Mississippi and, until 1844, the city's only parish church. It was named a basilica in 1961.
arch: Greek Revival in limestone, with a columned portico and a square tower with a steeple. Over the entrance a Latin inscription reads, in English, "In honor of St. Louis. Dedicated to the one and triune God. A.D. 1834".
features: When the riverfront was cleared for the Gateway Arch, every neighbouring building was demolished but the Old Cathedral was kept.
Hebrew letters spelling the divine name are inscribed above the main entrance.

look.d: Now framed by the Gateway Arch, the steeple once ruled the riverfront.
Latin and Hebrew are carved over the door.

fun: It is one of the most popular wedding churches in the Archdiocese of St. Louis.
journal: The Old Cathedral under the Arch. Everything around it was cleared; it stayed.
